newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan, HK plan talks on post-handover sea links.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan, HK plan talks on post-handover sea links.

text.p: Taiwan and Hong Kong negotiators plan talks to discuss shipping links after the British colony reverts to communist China -- Taiwan's arch rival -- in July, a senior Taipei official said on Thursday.

Kao Koong-lian, vice chairman for the cabinet's Mainland Affairs Council, said Taiwan had authorised the semi-official Straits Exchange Foundation to hold talks in April with the Hong Kong Shipowners' Association.
Beijing has authorised the private Hong Kong association to undertake shipping talks with Taiwan.
"We are confident the issue can be resolved in April," Kao told reporters.
The sides would meet in Hong Kong or Taipei at a date that Kao would not specify.
Kao said Taiwan transport officials would join the talks in their private capacities as advisers to the foundation.
No mainland officials would take part, Taiwan's state radio quoted the Hong Kong association as saying.

Taiwan firms have urged Taipei to secure direct shipping links with Hong Kong to ensure there is no interruption of service when the territory reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30 after more than 150 years as a British colony.

Hong Kong is the main transit point for the more than US$30 billion in Taiwan investments that have poured into China since the late 1980s, when a political thaw unleashed unofficial Taiwan-China ties.
Taiwan has banned all direct contacts with China since 1949, when it was split from the communist mainland by a civil war.
Beijing's Ministry of Communications on Wednesday approved five mainland firms to begin direct shipping links between the mainland port of Xiamen and Taiwan's Kaohsiung.
Taiwan's transport ministry said it would approve such sailings by mainland vessels that submit applications, and that crossings could begin as early as 10 days from Thursday.
Taipei does not regard the new service as a "direct shipping link" but rather an "offshore transshipment" scheme because mainland cargoes will not be allowed to enter Taiwan customs.
Rather, they can be processed in an "offshore" bonded zone in Kaohsiung outside of customs for onward shipment.
Taipei's conditions seek to ensure the breakthrough does not undermine the sovereignty of the island's exiled Republic of China, which does not recognise Beijing's sovereignty.
